limitations: Single shared-container JVM execution, not JMH, not a replicated statistical performance result.
All headline numbers are observed samples; they do not establish a universal speed, heap-size or scaling claim.
Default-capacity growth makes construction allocation include discarded intermediate arrays and tables.
M3 includes stable insertion order and flag columns; Apache HashMultiSet and Eclipse HashBag do not offer that feature combination.
Allocation meters exclude work on GC/JIT threads and do not measure retained graph size.
Current-thread CPU excludes CPU of other threads; wall time can include pauses and scheduling delays.
No JNI kernel, native memory, concurrency, null keys, full removals, provider views, bulk operations, presizing or large-count overflow measured.
Count samples use bounded positive counts for common semantics; existing separate differential tests own edge contracts.
Warmup is finite and does not prove every hot method has reached its final compilation tier.

The current class directory is a compiled diagnostic candidate that includes the proposed owner and two minimal constructor repairs; this evidence does not assert named-recipe application, product build, native/JNI proof or promotion.
CPU differences from the earlier class closure were observed in separate JVM executions and cannot be causally assigned to the rebase. No optimization or additional timing sweep was performed.
